method: Complete reads of five pinned test files; Git blob identities verified against pinned tree and SHA256 recorded. Upstream tests not executed.
findings: Size tests assert scalar/range thresholds, inclusive equal bounds, uint64 maximum and invalid overflow/range failures. They do not cover fractional leading zeros implicated by our earlier original-parser control. Most positive checks assert footer duplicate counts rather than path partitions.

Directory-size filtering test depends on directory st_size behavior and skips incompatible filesystems. Replay size test deliberately retains empty-file and empty-directory lint despite a positive minimum duplicate-file size.

mtime-window tests distinguish disabled, exact, subsecond and positive windows, chained timestamps and content-group boundaries. These are explicit membership policies, not evidence that matching timestamps prove content equality.

Newer-than tests document a fast-execution assumption, use wall clock, future mtimes and a three-second sleep. Updating stamp files makes repeated pedantic runs inappropriate; tests call run_rmlint_once.
Hidden-directory tests cover exclusion, explicit hidden roots and partial-hidden directory matching, using footer counts and some path/type assertions.

Permission test simply returns when root rather than pytest.skip, so a reported pass can contain no assertions. Non-root cases enumerate permission combinations and assert aggregate counts, not path identities.

local_verification.scope: Existing test uses a 100-byte file with max_file_bytes=99, max_depth=0 and max_entries=0. Each must report incomplete with an explicit Limit issue. Does not prove all threshold boundaries.

limits: No new production optimization or all-platform coverage claimed.
Repository remains partially reviewed; skipped native pHash/ASAN item untouched.
